author: Vieillot, 1808
summary: 드물게 찾아오는 길잃은새로, 대형 때까치류에 속하며 주로 혼자 또는 암수가 함께 지낸다. 주로 동물성 먹이를 먹어 설치류, 참새류 같은 작은 새, 개구리류와 파충류를 즐겨 잡고 곤충과 거미도 먹는다. 교목이나 관목 가지 위에 둥지를 틀고 한배에 알을 5~7개, 때로는 8~9개 낳는다.

art.subject: Northern Shrike (Lanius borealis), adult male in winter, as seen in Korean open country from November to February: crown, nape and back pale grey, with a narrow whitish band at the very front of the forehead; a black mask that is thin over the lores and broadens behind the eye over the ear coverts, with only a thin whitish line above it; chin, throat and cheeks white; outer scapulars whitish, forming a pale line along the edge of the back; rump paler grey; wings black with a small white patch at the base of the primaries; tail black with white outer feathers; underparts whitish with fine grey vermiculation across the breast and flanks; bill black with a strong hooked tip; iris dark brown; legs black.
art.pose: perched upright on top of a bare shrub, scanning for prey
art.scene: Korean winter open country with scattered trees and shrubs; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched upright: pale grey crown and back, narrow white forehead edge, black mask thin over the lores and broad behind the eye with a thin white line above, white chin, throat and cheeks, whitish outer scapulars, black wings with a small white primary patch, black tail with white edges, fine grey barring on the whitish breast, black hooked bill, black legs

first-winter, side view perched: brownish-grey crown and back, dark brown mask mainly behind the eye, faint pale supercilium, pale base to the lower mandible, buff-white underparts densely vermiculated grey-brown, blackish-brown wings with a small white primary patch
art.build: Large shrike, about 24.5cm, clearly larger than Bull-headed Shrike and smaller than Chinese Grey Shrike, with a big rounded head, no crest (the crown feathers lie flat), a strong hooked bill and a long, slightly graduated tail. Bill shorter than the head, deep, with a strongly hooked tip. Legs short and black. Perches upright and conspicuously on treetops and bush tops. In flight the black wings show a single white patch at the base of the primaries and the black tail shows white outer edges.
avoid: Do not paint a very long tail and a large white wing panel spreading onto the secondaries; those belong to Chinese Grey Shrike (Lanius sphenocercus).
Do not paint a black band across the forehead joining the masks; that is Lesser Grey Shrike (Lanius minor).
Do not give the adult a broad black band through the lores or a bold white supercilium; the mask is thin in front of the eye and the line above it is thin.
Do not paint rufous upperparts or a rufous crown; those suit Brown or Bull-headed Shrike.
Do not paint a pink or orange breast.
